placements.why: The envelope reports an instrument's calibration frequency and its verification against reference plates — an organizational activity (calibrating and validating instruments) rather than a single fact. No strata category exists yet in this repo, and nothing in the empty existing structure covers instrument calibration as an organizational concern, so this is a NEW mint with no parent required.
placements.title: Instrument Calibration as an Organizational Category
placements.theme: Observatory instruments must be calibrated to a target specification and that calibration verified against trusted reference data before the instrument is relied upon.

placements.title: Calibration Verification as the Basis for Instrument Trust
placements.theme: An instrument's calibration is only trustworthy once it has been checked against independent reference data and shown to hold across its full operating range.
placements.why: src-1/src-3 state the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration frequency (88.4 MHz) in prose and structured form; src-2/src-4 state that this calibration was verified against June reference plates and holds across the observing band. Per the position verdict these four segments form one paired report (what the calibration is, and how it was checked). The specific frequency and specific June-plate check are facts, but they evidence a recurring thematic subject — that instrument calibration must be independently verified before being trusted — which future calibration envelopes (other instruments, other verification runs) would keep feeding. No existing narrative leaf covers this (the graph is empty), so it is minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata rather than left as a bare fact.
